reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of relevance-based prediction hinges on defining a composite metric combining similarity and informativeness using Mahalanobis distances. This allows for capturing both how closely a draft prospect resembles previous players and how much information those players contribute relative to the average. The formulation uses inverse covariance matrices to normalize differences, ensuring that correlated variables do not skew results. The resulting relevance score serves as a weight in a weighted average of past outcomes, yielding predictions that are theoretically grounded in information theory and multivariate statistics. Unlike traditional linear regression, this method does not assume linearity but instead leverages kernel-based similarity. Failure modes include numerical instability when Ω is ill-conditioned or when sample sizes are too small compared to dimensionality. The system also introduces a 'fit' parameter that gauges confidence in individual predictions, allowing teams to calibrate their commitment levels accordingly.
